subject.title: feat(memory): carry source actor context into recall

question: Should OpenClaw accept sourceActor as a generic plugin SDK and memory recall attribution contract now, with Signal as the first producer, or defer/narrow it until the durable memory provenance model is designed?
rationale: The code path is technically plausible and well covered, but public plugin API expansion plus cross-channel memory attribution semantics require maintainer product/API intent; the branch is also currently conflicting.

options.title: Approve additive attribution contract
options.body: After the branch is rebased and prerequisites are landed or cleanly restacked, accept sourceActor as best-effort untrusted attribution metadata for plugins and memory supplements.

options.title: Narrow or defer public exposure
options.body: Ask the contributor to remove public memory/plugin sourceActor exposure and track the durable provenance or trust-enforcement design in the broader memory issues first.

options.title: Split after prerequisite merge
options.body: Require a fresh memory-only branch after the channel SourceActor prerequisite lands so this PR no longer carries Signal prerequisite changes.

recommendation.title: Approve additive attribution contract
recommendation.body: After the branch is rebased and prerequisites are landed or cleanly restacked, accept sourceActor as best-effort untrusted attribution metadata for plugins and memory supplements.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining question spans product/API direction and the cross-cutting runtime contract, and Peter Steinberger has the strongest recent history across the touched paths.
